subject: DPA redline: onshore backup carve-outs and deletion certification
messages:
From: Emma Jenkins <emma.jenkins@acmecorp.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 19 Jun 2024 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA: request for clarification on backups + deletion certification

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for sending the draft DPA. Our legal team flagged two things that need clarification before we can move to countersign:

1) Onshore backup carve-outs: Section 4.3 allows Redwood to retain backups for disaster recovery. We need to understand whether those backups can be stored outside the US and, if so, what controls exist. We are requesting an explicit onshore carve-out for backups containing Acme customer data or, alternatively, a commitment that backups with Acme data will only be stored in US regions.

2) Deletion certification: We require a process to verify deletions on demand (erasure requests). The clause in 5.2 says Redwood will "delete customer data" but does not mention a certification or timestamped evidence that can be shared for audit. Can you provide an example of the deletion certificate (format and contents) and whether that includes retention logs or proof of backup purges?

We also have a short list of examples we can share of acceptable deletion evidence. Would you mind looping in legal at your side and any engineering contact who owns backups? We are aiming to finalize this week.

Best,
Emma
Emma Jenkins
Senior Counsel, Acme Corp

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: DPA: request for clarification on backups + deletion certification

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Grace (legal) and Marcus (infrastructure) to confirm specifics.

Short answers up front:
- Backups: Redwood's default behavior is to keep backups in the same region as the primary tenant data unless a customer requests cross-region replication for DR. We can commit to keeping Acme backups in US-only regions as a DPA addendum.
- Deletion certification: We can provide a time-stamped deletion certificate that includes record IDs, deletion request ID, and a hash summary of the deleted objects. For backups we typically rely on tombstoning + scheduled purges; Marcus can outline how we produce proof of purge for backups and the expected timeline.

Marcus/Grace — can you confirm the language we should propose for the redline (i.e., "Backups containing Customer Data will be stored in US regions only unless Customer authorizes cross-region replication in writing" and a deletion-cert template reference)?

Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: DPA: request for clarification on backups + deletion certification

Jordan / Grace,

Quick technical summary and what we can commit to:

1) Backup residency: We run daily snapshots and incrementals. For customers requesting onshore-only, we can add a provisioning flag that pins snapshot storage to US regions (AWS us-east-1 or us-west-2). That means both primary and backup objects will be constrained to an approved US bucket. We cannot retroactively move historical backups without a separate migration/process and associated windows, but new backups after the flag is set will be US-only.

2) Backup purges: Our normal erase process marks objects as deleted, then a background purge job removes them from cold storage over a retention window (default 30 days for backups). We can accelerate that window for Acme to 7 days post-erase request for backup objects that are in our managed storage (note: this excludes third-party snapshot copies held by cloud provider for a short replication window — we will document those exceptions).

3) Deletion certificate: We can provide a signed JSON/CSV artifact with fields: customer_id, object_ids (list), deletion_request_id, timestamp_utc, operation_type (primary/delete/purge), and a sha256 summary. For backups, the certificate will state the purge job run timestamp and bucket/region where objects were purged.

Action items:
- Grace: propose short legal wording that combines the residency pin + an explicit carve-out for legacy snapshots with an agreed migration plan.
- Jordan: Once we have wording, I'll add the exact technical caveats so Acme understands the timelines.

Marcus
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Jun 2024 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft redline language for Acme (residency + deletion cert)

Team — drafting language below for Jordan to send to Acme. Kept it concise to reduce back-and-forth. Please confirm you can implement the commitments as written.

Proposed clause (to add to Section 4 - Data Location & Backups):
"Backups. Subject to Customer's purchase of an onshore backup option, Redwood will provision backup storage for Customer Data in United States regions only (US-East or US-West). For clarity, backups created after the effective date of Customer's onshore option will be stored onshore; Redwood will not be obligated to migrate pre-existing backups created prior to Customer's onshore election, but will provide a migration plan and timeline upon request. Redwood will expedite purge of backup objects associated with an approved Deletion Request to a maximum of 7 calendar days from issuance of the Deletion Request, except for brief replication artifacts created by the cloud provider for which Redwood has no direct control."

Proposed clause (to add to Section 5 - Deletion & Certification):
"Deletion Certification. Upon Customer's approved Deletion Request, Redwood will provide a signed Deletion Certificate within 5 business days. The Certificate will include: Deletion Request ID; a list of object identifiers or dataset names subject to deletion; UTC timestamp(s) for deletion and purge operations; operation type(s) (primary delete, backup purge); region(s) where purge occurred; and a sha256 summary for the deleted dataset. Where backup purge requires additional time as set forth in the Backups clause above, the Certificate will include the expected completion date for backup purge and a subsequent confirmation once purge is complete."

If that language looks good to you Marcus, Jordan, I'll fold it into the redline doc and send to Acme.

Grace
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: DPA redline - onshore backups and deletion certification (proposed)

Emma — attaching a concise redline that incorporates the onshore backup option and Deletion Certificate language we discussed. Highlights:
- We will provision backups to US regions for Acme upon election of the onshore backup option (no automatic migration of historical backups; migration plan available).
- We commit to expedited backup purge within 7 calendar days for managed backups and will include the backup purge status in the signed Deletion Certificate.
- Deletion Certificate template included in the redline appendix; Redwood will deliver the certificate within 5 business days of an approved request, and a follow-up confirmation once backup purge completes.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm Acme is comfortable with the onshore-option model vs. an unconditional retroactive migration.
2) If yes, we can finalize the addendum and circulate for countersignature.

Attached: DPA_Redline_Acme-v2.docx (redline)

Thanks —
Jordan
